newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mixed on Tuesday due to an uncertain short-term market trend, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 19,450 yuan ($2,344) per tonne, unchanged from Monday's close. It opened at an intra-day low of 19,250 and hit a high of 19,500.

October rose 20 to 19,340 yuan per tonne, November fell 10 to 19,290, December was unchanged at 19,350, January dropped 10 to 19,410, March was up 100 to 19,600, April 50 to 19,600 and May decreased 150 to 19,650.
Combined volume fell to 55,400 tonnes from 73,890.
Copper opened lower on overnight losses on the LME but short-covering and speculative buying pushed the prices back for most of the session.
"Copper on the LME did not move out of the key range of $1,900-$1,970 despite overnight losses and Shanghai speculators preferred to take profits at low levels," one trader said.
"Short position holders did not wanted to enlarge their positions at low levels with short-term market trend unclear," he added.
Traders said market sentiment was poor due to a domestic over-surplus of spot copper but further falls need LME help.
"Shanghai copper will not drop sharply until the LME breach the $1,900 level," a second trader said.
Analysts expect copper to move around 19,500 yuan in the short term.
Aluminium end mixed. October fell 80 to 13,500 yuan, November was unchanged at 13,600, December rose 50 to 13,450 and January fell 300 to 13,000.
Combined volume rose to 1,480 tonnes from 1,410.
